title: DTLS handshake signature scheme confusion allows peer impersonation
summary: The verifier selected its primitive from the certificate key type but its digest from the peer-controlled handshake scheme, allowing a forged signature to bypass proof of private-key possession. An attacker able to redirect a DTLS handshake and access the peer public certificate may impersonate that peer. The advisory says WebRTC SDP fingerprint checking does not stop this attack.
ai_role: The Pion maintainer's case-specific advisory credits Anthropic's OSS Scanner as discoverer (tracking identifier 0Q4PYECH). It does not identify model versions or internal discovery dates.
classification_note: The cited advisory documents public disclosure; it does not establish whether defenders knew of the issue or whether it was exploited before disclosure.
remediation_note: The advisory identifies fix commit cb56053 and the following package-version scope: v2 2.0.0–2.2.12 (no patched v2 version listed); v3 before 3.1.13, fixed 3.1.13. This source does not establish downstream deployment.

impacts.conditions: An attacker able to redirect a DTLS handshake and access the peer’s public certificate may impersonate that peer without its private key.
impacts.exploitation: The advisory describes a possible attack path but does not report observed exploitation.
